annotations.title: Check a wallet for blacklists, freezes and government sanctions

description: Check one wallet address against both the on-chain record of stablecoin blacklists, freezes and seizures and official government sanctions lists. Returns a Sanctions & Blacklist Report for supported smart-contract wallets, with every recorded issuer action (which issuer took it, on which blockchain, on what date, and in which transaction and block, so it can be checked independently) alongside the per-agency government sanctions result. For Bitcoin and Bitcoin-family addresses, which have no on-chain stablecoin blacklists, returns a Government Sanctions Report only. Covers USDT, USDC and every other coin in this record, on every blockchain it checks, plus official government sanctions lists. Returns dated public records only, never a risk score, rating, or opinion about the address or its owner, and does not check money laundering, related wallets, or wallet ownership. Needs no account.

address.description: The wallet address to check, in any format the chain uses. Accepts Ethereum-style addresses (used by Ethereum and many other chains), addresses on Tron, Solana, Stellar, TON, the XRP Ledger, Aptos, Starknet, Sui and the TX Chain, and NEAR account names that end in .near for both stablecoin blacklists and government sanctions, plus Bitcoin, Bitcoin Cash, Bitcoin Gold, Litecoin, Dogecoin, Dash, Zcash and Monero addresses for government sanctions only (these networks have no on-chain stablecoin blacklists). An Ethereum-style address works in all small letters, all capitals, or with the capitals the wallet shows. Any other mix of capitals is read as a typo. For every other kind of address, keep the capital and small letters as the wallet shows them.
